what: The 6-byte Primorial-Fold transport. Predictions committed BEFORE the measurement ran (seal-before-measure). Measured by fallairgap.mjs measure(), counted in real UTF-8 wire bytes.
codec: SENTINEL (vendored, mutation-gated) — Thomas Frumkin's Konomi primorial-fold codec

predictions.claim: Every event's 6-byte PAYLOAD beats its self-describing JSON by at least 20x (the coordinate regime). We predicted 20-40x, not Simon's headline 42x, because our canonical JSON is leaner than his 252-byte example.
A recurring deterministic step sent as a 1-byte delta (heartbeat, pipeline_step) beats JSON by at least 100x (the 100x+ regime).

Signed PER-PACKET, the 71-byte wire vs apples-to-apples signed JSON is UNDER 10x. The 64-byte Ed25519 signature dominates, proving the 42-100x is only realised when the signature is AMORTISED over a session, never per packet. This is the honest limit the 15x test never measured.
A raw Ed25519 signature (64B) and a SHA-256 hash (32B) do not compress past their entropy floor.
predictions.pass_if: entropyFloor lists signature=64 and hash=32 both compresses:false

predictions.claim: A forged or tampered signed frame is dropped by the signature-first gate BEFORE its payload is parsed; a valid frame round-trips. No forged frame ever compiles to a command.
predictions.pass_if: sigFirstDrop + SENTINEL check reject forged before parse, accept valid

predictions.claim: All 5 sample event types encode to 6 bytes and decode back to the same event type (codec is total and reversible for the event set).
